Idle residency defaults to 128 quiescent engines in an LRU idle set; engines with active collectors, in-flight work, or an in-flight fetch are never evicted.
50 concurrent getters plus 50 collectors demanding one key produce exactly one fetch, and all 100 observe its outcome.
A NotModified response surfaces as exactly one Revalidated(age) and clears staleness, not as a redundant Data frame.

Zero configuration and explicit expert configuration are byte-identical in behavior, with the equivalence asserted over persistence, bookkeeper, freshness validator, and idle cap — not telemetry or overlay.

The engine performs zero retries and zero backoff; a failed refresh schedules nothing and a later call is new demand
A key's namespace and canonicalId() together form its stable identity, and implementations should return the same identity components for the lifetime of the key
canonicalId is the deduplication lever: two keys with the same namespace and canonical id share one in-flight fetch, one resident value, one stale mark
namespace is the unit of bulk operations, and the durable watermark it carries covers keys the store has never seen
The canonical id must not contain request-varying noise (timestamps, request ids, nonces) or secrets, because it is a cache key written to the source of truth
Invalidating a namespace before a key has ever been fetched still makes that key's first read honest, because namespace and global watermarks are durable

Every StoreError message states what was attempted, for which key or namespace, and the likely fix

maxIdleKeys bounds the LRU idle set of quiescent engines, defaults to 128, requires count >= 0, and 0 destroys every engine at quiescence

Eviction discards only derived in-memory state — durable rows, freshness metadata, stale marks, and watermarks live in the source of truth and bookkeeper — so a later read of an evicted key is semantically identical to one never evicted

Graduation to stable is gated, not scheduled: first review at 6.1, target window roughly 6.3, requiring the API unchanged across two consecutive minors, green crash-matrix and soak lanes, and at least three external production adopters.

The non-transactional acknowledgement path adopts the server echo first and retires the journal row last, so a crash inside the ack window can re-send the same push; server endpoints must be idempotent or keyed by mutation identity, and closing the window is beta01 work.

mutate appends one typed intent to the journal and returns an opaque mutation id correlating it with pending, pendingWrites, deadLetters, and intent events; a ref from a foreign registry throws IllegalArgumentException.
The engine-owned overlay projects confirmed residence through pending intents, and Store stamps a changed projection with OVERLAY origin, zero age, and no staleness.
get on a MutationStore is never projected by the overlay; overlays apply only to stream.

mutationStore takes exactly five required factory inputs — registry, server, keyResolver, valueCodecVersion, valueCodec — plus a configure lambda; optional Store configuration never moves onto the factory parameters.
valueCodecVersion must be positive; the factory rejects non-positive versions with IllegalArgumentException before construction.
The configure lambda must install a fetcher { }, fetcherOfResult { }, or fetcher(Fetcher) door; omitting all three fails with a message saying so.
MutationStoreBuilder deliberately exposes no overlay door: the mutation engine's overlay is a mutation store's sole projection layer and is installed by the factory.
For keys reconstructible from the identity pair, the required key resolver is one line building K from identity.canonicalId.

Unset persistence and bookkeeper doors install one mutations-owned in-memory default each, forwarded identically to both the delegated core Store and the mutation engine; core's inaccessible internal defaults are never silently substituted.

After mutate, stream emits the optimistic value with origin OVERLAY; after a drained acknowledgement the server echo becomes the committed value attributed SOT or MEMORY, and a stream opened after the acknowledgement sees the echo — convergence for a collector already active across the acknowledgement is not yet promised.
update registrations decline when the confirmed base is Absent; the projector transforms an existing value only.

delete accepts neither a version nor a codec: Store 6 owns a fixed version-1 Unit codec whose encoding is exactly zero bytes, and durable delete rows with another version or non-empty bytes are a CODEC failure.
upsert receives the explicit confirmed presence and must return a presence — it cannot decline.
Returning null from a projector means exactly 'decline this intent'; deletion is MutationPresence.Absent, never null; and a declined head remains pending, blocking only its same-effective-key suffix.

A projector must be a pure, deterministic, non-blocking function of (base, args) that never calls back into Store; a thrown failure is contained, reported through MutationStore.poisoned, and parks the row with a normalized PROJECTION failure.
A MutatorRef belonging to a different registry instance fails mutate with IllegalArgumentException — refs are ownership-validated by registry identity, not id-matched.

Codec decode receives the persisted version, which may be older than the currently registered one; format changes append a version, and old decoders remain until the corresponding rows are retired and pruned.

stales must be pure (equal inputs produce structurally equal StaleSets); its result is copied, normalized to identity pairs, deduplicated, and sorted into immutable durable effect records before the intent's first push.
A pending-write affordance keys on origin == OVERLAY and a stale-cache affordance keys on isStale — two distinct affordances that must not be swapped.

isStale is never set on an OVERLAY frame: overlay frames are stamped age = Duration.ZERO and isStale = false unconditionally, with only refreshing live, so an isStale-driven spinner will never fire for a pending write.
Store.get is unprojected — overlays apply only to stream — so observing your own optimistic write requires collecting stream.

The overlay projection table defines optimistic create and delete: a non-null result over a null base emits overlay data, and a null result over a non-null base exposes the normal absent/loading transition.
pending(key) returns the current pending intents for the key's terminal canonical identity in durable client-sequence FIFO order, providing durable data for richer saving affordances.
The events flow is read-only, in-process, and advisory: replay 0, extra buffer capacity 64, DROP_OLDEST overflow — suitable for transient UI but never for settlement logic.
Retries of one MutationPush.idempotencyKey must be idempotent: a duplicate success must return the same authoritative presence, value, etag, and canonical target.
A precondition conflict is signalled only by throwing StoreResults.exception(StoreResults.conflict(serverMeta, message), cause) — the sanctioned public core door.
A CancellationException thrown out of push is rethrown and leaves the INFLIGHT generation intact; the next explicit drain or restart sends the exact same immutable generation.

Only MutationPresentAck can carry a canonicalKey (an optional same-namespace redirect), and a retry of one generation's idempotency key must return the same canonical target or the intent parks as a protocol violation.

MutationAbsentAck deliberately has no canonical key, making rekey-on-deletion unrepresentable, and certifies the deletion-coherence obligation: every fetch begun after an Absent acknowledgement returns FetcherResult.Deleted — tombstones stop journal replay but do not mask a violating backend.

Retirement confirmation must be monotonic and cannot exceed the requested prefix; the library validates both properties and treats a violation as a protocol failure, and cancellation during retire leaves the confirmed prefix unchanged and prunes nothing.

A crash inside the ack window re-sends the same push after restart because the alpha adopts the echo first and retires the journal row last — design endpoints to be idempotent or keyed by mutation identity.
baseMeta == null never means an unconditional write: the frozen base itself is always an existence/value precondition.
Without a registered merge policy, server-wins is the non-removable conflict terminal; there is deliberately no terminal setter.
The precondition selector runs once per newly prepared semantic generation and never on a transport retry.

Returning null from the precondition selector deliberately selects an existence/value precondition without metadata and never removes the base precondition; without a selector, the candidate's captured metadata is selected.

MutationConflictResolution.Retry persists generation g+1 before transmission — with a new idempotency key, since idempotency keys are generation-stable — while ServerWins retires the intent without another push.

On the third consecutive conflict receipt carrying identical server metadata, the intent parks with a normalized CONFLICT failure instead of preparing another generation, and a merge that throws parks the intent as well.
Within one conflicts block, each policy (precondition, merge) registers at most once; a second registration fails.
A durable invalidation effect skipped by conflict server-wins reaches the terminal SKIPPED disposition and is reported by the advisory MutationEffectSkipped event.
drain(key) is one idempotent, scheduler-agnostic foreground pass that pushes the pending FIFO prefix once with no retry or backoff, and the pass never fetches.

Global drain enumerates every durable identity from the journal and reconstructs it through the required resolver; an identity that fails to resolve parks its affected pre-ack head without blocking others, and processing is deterministic by durable client sequence within an effective identity with no cross-key order promise.

Once transport becomes possible or uncertain, that durable execution owns its client namespace until it parks or retires: a keyed drain for another key in the same namespace returns without transport while different namespaces remain eligible to progress.
Durable key identity is exactly (namespace.value, canonicalId()); hashes, object identity, and key class are never durable identity.
Every resolver result is validated verbatim against the requested pair before any transport or adoption work; null and identity mismatch are rejected with descriptive failures.
The internal exponential backoff between scheduled retries uses base 1,000 ms capped at 300,000 ms, and no public policy door exists — explicit drain passes are the override.
Hydration rebuilds every process cache from one coherent durable snapshot, runs codec work only after the storage transaction returns, and never emits an overlay or alias revision.
Leaving the journalStorage door unset installs InMemoryMutationJournalStorage — the journal stays in memory, and restart hydration requires reopening a store over the same durable instance.

InMemoryMutationJournalStorage is intentionally non-durable across process death: a transaction operates on a private snapshot under one mutex, normal return replaces the committed snapshot, and any throw discards it.

SqlDelightMutationJournalStorage requires the driver and transacter to address the same connection/database (a pairing the library cannot verify), supports synchronous drivers only (async web drivers unsupported), and requires dedicating the driver or externally serializing other access.
The SqlDelight adapter's internal sidecar owns the store6_mutation_* schema with its own version row (current schema version 2, migrating version 1) and leaves SQLite user_version user-owned.
MutationJournalStorage and MutationJournalTransaction carry @SubclassOptInRequired(DelicateStoreApi::class), so implementing storage is a deliberate act.

The single transaction door is exception-atomic with a deliberately non-suspending callback: normal return commits every operation, any thrown Throwable including cancellation commits none, and codec/resolver/transport/policy work cannot run while the transaction is held.
The storage package freezes nine logical records, and implementations must persist enum names never ordinals, store times as Unix epoch milliseconds, and copy every byte array on entry and delivery.
Ordinary prune removes eligible records only at or below the persisted server-confirmed retirement prefix, and alias redirects plus active or pending tombstone generations are never removed by it.
pending(key) follows aliases as durable identity pairs only: it never reconstructs a K, never consults the resolver, and therefore cannot fail on an unresolvable canonical key.
Dead letters contain only PARKED entries; parking is legal only before a successful acknowledgement is durably recorded, and a parked sequence never re-enters the executable FIFO.

The five public pending states (PENDING, INFLIGHT, REFRESHING, ADOPTING, APPLYING_EFFECTS) are the total public mapping of the six nonterminal durable execution phases; parked executions appear only in dead letters and retired ones in neither inspection API.
MutationFailureKind is a broad, append-only classification with exactly nine classes: IDENTITY, CODEC, PROJECTION, PROTOCOL, CONFLICT, TRANSPORT, ADOPTION, EFFECT, PERSISTENCE.

A raw StoreError or Throwable is never persisted in a MutationFailure; detail is at most 128 and message at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, each truncated at a code-point boundary after control-character and stack-trace sanitization.

The events flow delivers best-effort advisory telemetry — replay 0, extra buffer capacity 64, oldest dropped on overflow, tryEmit-only — and is never a drain, acknowledgement, retry, or settlement protocol; no event carries a raw Throwable or StoreError.
The poisoned flow replays 16 entries with DROP_OLDEST and carries the exact projection Throwable in-process only; the same throw parks the row with a normalized durable PROJECTION failure.

MutationJournalStorageContractKit is extended with createStorage() and reopenStorage(previous); reopenStorage is the restart boundary — an in-memory implementation returns the same instance while a persistent one returns a new adapter over the same durable store.

The kit enforces named phase rules rather than a false total ordering: INFLIGHT -> READY is legal after a transport failure, REFRESH_REQUIRED may advance to a new immutable generation before returning to READY, RETIRED and PARKED are terminal, and ACKED/EFFECTS_PENDING never regress to a pre-ack phase.
The contract kit inherits the deterministic kill-point crash scenarios, so extending it runs them automatically.

KillPointJournalStorage is a one-shot deterministic crash decorator with five semantic boundaries around retirement finalization and prune; arm rejects a second armed point, the armed point clears before its crash is raised, and classification never depends on transaction ordinals or scheduler timing.
The purity kit's double-application test compares two independent two-step replay traces and does not require idempotence, which would incorrectly reject lawful append and increment mutators.
snapshotValue must return detached structural data suitable for equality checks because MutationPresence.Present deliberately does not define structural equality.
mutatorPuritySubject requires at least one base/args sample and at least one named ambient-state probe, with unique names for each.

Store 6 stream emits fetcher and source-of-truth failures as StoreResult.Error values rather than throwing; only a MustBeFresh initial-cycle fetch or revalidation failure emits one error and completes the flow.
store<K, V> { } without a fetcher registration fails at build time with IllegalArgumentException; installing a source of truth does not substitute for a fetcher.

Freshness is a per-call sealed policy with exactly five variants; LocalOnly never invokes the fetcher, probes the source of truth once on a memory miss, and reports StoreError.Missing when nothing is local.
The engine performs zero retries and zero backoff at zero configuration; one demand cycle invokes the fetcher exactly once and retries belong in the user's fetcher.
MutationStore implements Store by delegation while withholding the raw engine write handle: runtime() on it returns null so every consumer write stays journalled.
isStale is never set on an OVERLAY frame (overlay frames are stamped age = Duration.ZERO and isStale = false unconditionally), and Store.get is unprojected — overlays apply only to stream.
The Store 6 seam is the package for plugging in a fetcher, source of truth, bookkeeper, clock, telemetry, or overlay — there is no converter role among the seam files.
Store 5's Converter bridges network, local, and output model types via fromNetworkToLocal and fromOutputToLocal; Store 6 has no such interface and types the store on a single value type.

In Store 6 the value-to-row mapping lives in adapter callbacks: SqlDelightSourceOfTruth's constructor takes readQuery, writeRow, deleteRow, deleteNamespaceRows, and deleteAllRows lambdas over generated queries.

Store 6's FetcherResult vocabulary is Success(value, etag), NotModified(etag), Error(cause), and Deleted — adding conditional-fetch and server-deletion variants over Store 5's Data/Error set, with Deleted clearing residence and triggering no automatic refetch.

Store 5's Validator exposes a per-item suspend isValid(item) hook; Store 6's seam FreshnessValidator is instead a pure read planner whose plan(context) returns a FetchPlan (Skip, Fetch, or Conditional).

MutationServer, the app-owned transport replacing Updater.post, has exactly two methods — push(request): MutationAck and retire(request): MutationRetirementAck — and retries of one idempotency key must be idempotent.

MutatorRegistryBuilder offers update, create, delete, and upsert registration shapes returning typed refs; update declines on an Absent base, delete always applies MutationPresence.Absent, and upsert cannot decline.

Store 6's seam Bookkeeper is durable freshness bookkeeping, not failed-sync tracking: one store-local monotone sequence shared by successes, stale marks, and watermarks, with a key durably stale exactly when max(mark/ns/global) > (success ?: 0).

Store 5's SourceOfTruth carries three type parameters (Key, Local, Output) and exposes reader(key): Flow<Output?>, write, delete, and deleteAll.
